about: cesr.parse cases that a parser must accept, carried the way CESR carries them: a genus/version code, then KERI message bodies framed by their version strings, each followed by attachment groups in the attachments group (-C) the master table defines for them. The bodies are KERI inception events built to the KERI specification (v1.0.1, commit 71cb54ebb445dd9d8cb33cd29a5f50894fafc569, 'Inception Event Message Body': fields [ v, t, d, i, s, kt, k, nt, n, bt, b, c, a], all required) with d and i computed by the CESR SAID protocol using Blake3-256; keys, digests and signatures are fixed SHAKE-256 bytes, so signatures do not verify and these cases say nothing about KERI validity beyond well-formed bodies. Every counter reports group_end, where the group it introduces ends.

cases.title: Frame a KERI 2.0 JSON inception by its version string, then its signatures
cases.description: A genus/version code, a KERI 2.0 inception body (JSON, version string KERICAACAAJSON, SAIDs computed by the CESR SAID protocol), then an attachments group (-C) holding a controller signature group (-K) of two Ed25519 indexed signatures (code A#, index only). The parser must take the body's length from its version string to find where the attachments begin.

cases.title: Parse a big current-only Ed25519 signature whose ondex field is not zero
cases.description: Code 2B#### with index 70 and ondex 9. The table row defines a two-character ondex field for this current-only code and states no constraint on its value, so the decoded structure reports the ondex as encoded.

assertions.note: spec-conflict: count-code size counts quadlets/triplets (line 591) vs 'count of the following Primitives or groups' (legends at lines 674 and 714, Examples at line 1103)

dispute.summary: The Annex indexed code table gives 2B#### (Ed25519 indexed sig big current only) an ondex field of two characters and states no constraint on its value, so a stream carrying ondex 9 decodes to index 70, ondex 9. keripy main (9a8b7aa7) rejects it: Indexer raises 'Invalid ondex=9 for code=2B' because keripy requires the ondex of every current-only code to be zero (src/keri/core/indexing.py, the IdxCrtSigDex checks in _exfil and _bexfil). The question has a KERI-layer dimension (review finding SEC-F4): neither the CESR nor the KERI specification says what an ondex on a current-only signature means, and keripy's own semantics exist only in its CESR layer, while its KERI-layer exposeds() indexes the prior next-key digests with whatever ondex a signature carries. An implementation that decodes the field as the table allows and reuses that KERI logic could count a current-only signature toward the prior-next threshold where keripy rejects the stream, so validators could disagree about one controller-signed event. The review's verifier judged this a controller-induced interop divergence rather than a way for an unauthorized key to gain weight. The specification should state whether a current-only code's ondex must be zero (making this a must-reject stream under a new case id) or what it means.
dispute.raised_at: generators/DISAGREEMENTS.md in this repository, 2026-10-01, and the KERI review panel of the CESR catalogue (finding SEC-F4); not yet raised with the CESR specification working group.

cases.title: A signature group's size counts quadlets, not signatures
cases.description: The founding case of the suite. After a KERI 2.0 inception, an attachments group (-C) holds a controller signature group (-K) of three Ed25519 indexed signatures and then a witness signature group (-L) of one. -K has size 66 (3 x 22 quadlets), not 3; -L has size 22, not 1; -C has size 90. A second inception and its attachments follow. A parser that counts items reads 66 as 66 signatures, runs past -K and loses the stream. The symbol legends of the Encoding Scheme Symbols Table (line 674) and the indexed-code symbol table (line 714), and the Examples text at line 1103, say a count code's digits count 'Primitives or groups'; this case rests on the explicit rule at line 591 instead.

cases.title: A nested signature group's quadlets count toward its enclosing group
cases.description: The shape of the specification's own Examples (lines 1104-1116): a transferable indexed signature groups code (-X) whose group holds a prefix (E), a sequence number (0A), a digest (E) and a controller signature group (-K) of two signatures. -X's size, 73 (11 + 6 + 11 + 1 + 44), counts every quadlet including -K's code and contents; -K's is 44. The specification's example is built the same way: -XBf is 95 = 11 + 6 + 11 + 1 + 66. The symbol legends of the Encoding Scheme Symbols Table (line 674) and the indexed-code symbol table (line 714), and the Examples text at line 1103, say a count code's digits count 'Primitives or groups'; this case rests on the explicit rule at line 591 instead.

dispute.summary: The specification lets a count code count zero quadlets (the small count code's two size characters provide 'counts from 0 to 4095', and the size MUST count the quadlets in the group, which here are none), so an attachments group of size 0 after a body is well formed and ends at its own count code. keripy main (9a8b7aa7) rejects it: after taking the empty -C, msgParsator peeks for a genus/version code inside the group and the empty substream raises ShortageError, reported as SizedGroupError (src/keri/core/parsing.py, the 'peek for version change' extraction after AttachmentGroup). keripy's own comment there says a message with no attachments MUST have at least an empty AttachmentGroup, so this looks like a keripy defect rather than a reading of the text; it rejects a stream, so it is not a security matter.
dispute.raised_at: generators/DISAGREEMENTS.md in this repository, 2026-10-01; not yet raised with keripy or the CESR specification working group.
